## Theorem: failed split proof replay

For the exact R247 suffix necessary predicate C_d, let c(S) count support labels on the original directed germ set S, with cap 2^d-1. The predicate rejects over-capacity, accepts c(S)<=d, and otherwise searches the frozen split library (necessary walls if saturated, full library otherwise). For each rejected split choose one rejected child, and a witness subset W inside that child: if child is over capacity select one germ from each of 2^(d-1) distinct labels; otherwise recursively replay the negative memo of that child. Take the union U of those witnesses, then add original germs so that c(U)>=d+1 in the unsaturated case, or c(U)=2^d-1 in the saturated case. For a directly over-capacity parent use 2^d labels instead. By induction and R303 heredity, every split still has a failed child on U. U is a subset of S, stays below saturation if S was unsaturated, and remains saturated if S was saturated, so the same split library applies; padding also prevents the c<=d optimistic shortcut. Hence C_d(U)=false. The empty branch never requires a failure witness. This proof uses the actual zero-containing split pairs and does not assign unobserved germs to either side. No minimum-core assertion. Replay requires no new recursive feasibility solves; its split visits, label-cover work and optional separate verification are additional costs. The code prefers already selected germs when covering a capacity leaf. The first 128 newly solved root failures are extracted; the rest retain full cores. A bounded second predicate with a separate memo checks a deterministic sample of extracted roots. The index includes R305's historical full roots and the new small cores are queried on historical index misses; unknowns are retained, including after the solving ceiling.
